summary: Outer end of the Burlington Canal's south pier: a range light in line with the stone main light; concrete tower of 1939, green, automated 1987; tower closed to visitors.

structures.note: Open frame steel skeleton tower, square, painted red, 36 ft (11 m) high (Department report, fiscal 1905, pp. 38-39). Tower supplied by Gould, Shapley & Muir, Brantford, at $356 (same report; Lighthouse Friends gives the same firm and price). Erection by days' labour under W. K. Morris, $523.56 (report).
Forty-one feet (12.5 m), octagonal, with octagonal iron lantern (Lighthouse Friends); erected 1909 with E. P. Jennings engaged on the work (fiscal 1910 report, scan 69). Replaced in 1939.
White square tower with green top (Coast Guard entry 535). BCLG: four-sided tapered concrete structure.

access.note: Pier reached from the parking lot at the south end of the lift bridge. Grounds open; tower closed (Lighthouse Friends).

visit.note: Working navigation light, shown seasonally (Coast Guard list); the tower is closed to visitors.

events.note: Canal lights erected in the 1832 season (William J. Kerr). Not specific to the front range.
New front range set at the end of the pier, a square wooden tower 14 ft tall (Lighthouse Friends). BCLG dates a wooden front light at the end of the western south pier to 1856. Disputed.
Steamship Ranger set a pier alight on 18 July 1856; the fire destroyed the octagonal canal lighthouse and other nearby structures (Lighthouse Friends).
Small fire in the lantern room of the outer pierhead light after a duck overturned the lamp; Keeper Campbell put it out (Lighthouse Friends, citing a newspaper account not read).

Open frame steel tower, 11 m (36 ft) high, fixed white dioptric 7th-order light 12 m (39 ft) above the lake, visible 11 miles. Tower supplied by Gould, Shapley & Muir at $356; erection by days' labour under W. K. Morris, $523.56 (fiscal 1905 report). Lighthouse Friends gives the same firm and $356.

Early December 1907 storm heavily damaged the piers at the entrance; temporary pole lights set while the south pier was rebuilt (Lighthouse Friends). The fiscal 1908 report lists a temporary pole light at Burlington beach.
Reinforced concrete octagonal tower built on the pier by department staff under E. P. Jennings (fiscal 1910 report). BCLG says the tower replaced the earlier front light in 1910.
Range lights on masts discontinued; new tower with a dioptric 4th-order 360 degree lens showing a fixed red light (fiscal 1910 report).

1-inch single diaphone plant with a 3-h.p. gasoline engine at Burlington beach (fiscal 1910 works list, scan 84): machinery furnished under general contract by Can. Fog Signal Co., Toronto ($1,170.00); installation a separate item. Lighthouse Friends says the diaphone was installed inside the new tower. Location disputed.
Light and fog signal electrified (BCLG; Lighthouse Friends). A fiscal 1923 works list has Installation of electric lights and electrically driven fog alarm at Burlington, without naming the tower.
Present four-sided tapered concrete tower built; Lighthouse Friends says it carried a fixed green light and an electric tyfon horn.
Canal lights automated 1987 (Lighthouse Friends) and keeper's dwelling left vacant; the Beach Canal Lighthouse Group gives 1990.

corrections.why: Fl R 4s is Coast Guard entry 533, Burlington Canal North Pier Outer (on the west side of the canal). The record's coordinates (43.301002, -79.790496) match entry 535, Burlington Canal South Pier Outer, which is Iso G 4s with a green top. The record's own tower height (13.1 m) and CCG tower number already come from entry 535.
9.1 m is entry 533 (North Pier Outer). Entry 535 (South Pier Outer, the front range) gives a focal height of 14.5 m.
The 4 nm range is entry 533. Entry 535 gives 10 nautical miles.
The record's Coast Guard number for the front range is I533 (North Pier Outer). The front range's own entry is I535, Burlington Canal South Pier Outer, at the record's coordinates.

No source read gives 1842. Lighthouse Friends dates the new front range to 1845, BCLG dates a wooden front light to 1856, and Lighthouse Friends dates the first canal lights to the 1832 season. The proposed 1845 is Lighthouse Friends's date and is disputed by BCLG. A human should decide.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Rowlett's 1909 build date matches the fiscal 1910 report, which says the concrete tower was erected in 1909 under E. P. Jennings and that the range lights on masts were then discontinued. BCLG's 1910 is the year it was lit and put in service, and is consistent with this. Resolved as built 1909, in service by 1910.

Not a disagreement. The fiscal 1905 report gives Gould, Shapley & Muir, Brantford, as supplier of the steel tower at $356, and days' labour under W. K. Morris at $523.56 for the work. Lighthouse Friends gives the same firm and $356.

Not reconciled. The fiscal 1910 works list places the 1-inch diaphone at Burlington beach, with the machinery furnished by Can. Fog Signal Co. and the installation a separate item (scan 84). Lighthouse Friends says it was installed inside the new tower.
Not reconciled. Lighthouse Friends gives 1987; the Beach Canal Lighthouse Group gives 1990 and says Coletti was transferred after it. The story gives both.

notes_for_editor: (1) IDENTITY: the record's light values and I533 are the Coast Guard entry for the North Pier Outer light (Fl R 4s, 9.1 m, 4 nm). The record's coordinates and 13.1 m tower match the South Pier Outer light (I535: Iso G 4s, 14.5 m, 10 nm). This story treats I535 as the front range, which fits the sources (outer end of the south pier, white square tower with green top since 1939). The corrections change the record's light data and need a human look. (2) FIRST LIGHT: 1842 (record; Rowlett) is not supported by any source read. Dates in play: 1832 (canal lights, Lighthouse Friends), 1845 (new front range, Lighthouse Friends), 1856 (wooden front light, BCLG). Not reconciled. (3) 1905 BUILDER: not a disagreement. The fiscal 1905 report (scan 43-44, printed pp. 38-39) gives the supply of the steel tower to Gould, Shapley & Muir at $356 and days' labour under W. K. Morris at $523.56. The fiscal year label convention applies: the 1905 report is for the year ended 30 June 1905. (4) 1909 VS 1910: the fiscal 1910 report and Lighthouse Friends give 1909; BCLG gives 1910. Used 1909 build, in service 1910. (5) OCR TABLE READS, checked against the page images on 2026-10-28: the Lundy keeper row (fiscal 1914, scan 74) reads 'Burlington bay, lights and fog alarm / T. Lundy / May 2, 1905 / 780 00' in the image, confirmed. The 1910 works list (scan 84) reads Burlington beach, item (1) diaphone machinery furnished by Can. Fog Signal Co. at $1,170.00, and item (2) installation as a separate item; the story corrected its earlier 'installed by' wording. Jennings's 1909 sentence is on scan 69; its printed page is unconfirmed, so the story cites scan page 69. (6) KEEPERS: Lighthouse Friends gives one keeper list for the canal lights, main light and front range together. The story no longer says the front range was tended by the same men; the sources do not split the keepers by light. Coletti: Lighthouse Friends gives 1968 to 1987, while the same page says he was keeper when the stone tower was decommissioned in 1961. Not resolved; the roster keeps the list's dates. (7) 1922: Lighthouse Friends and BCLG both say the front light and fog signal were electrified in 1922; the fiscal 1923 works list names Burlington without a tower. (8) The 1900 duck incident comes from Lighthouse Friends, which cites a newspaper account not read. (9) The 2021 heritage designation is for the main light according to Lighthouse Friends; the front range was not checked against the Canadian Register or the Parks Canada list. (10) The Thompson diary quotations are on the Lighthouse Friends page but are not used here; they belong to the main light's story. The main-light story (ca-on-burlington-canal-main) uses the same keeper list and should agree with this one. (11) Corpus keeper tables mention Campbell, Thos at Burlington Bay Lights (fiscal 1904), but that row is a position read and was not used. (12) Fact-check edits (2026-10-28): removed the unsourced 'none describes a separate plan' sentence; 'two dates have not been reconciled' now reads 'disagree'; 'more than once' replaced by LF's 'several occasions'; metre-first units for 12.5 m (41 ft); the temporary range lights are placed on the north pier per Lighthouse Friends; the 2003 sentence now follows LF's wording.
